text: Attempt 19: attempt 17's mixed layout with LIGHT homes (17 and 18 both stopped near 29,000 with dense homes outrunning jobs), more factory cells, the second seaport at ~20,000, and population reminders that stop the loop so no planned step is missed.
Day one, light homes (a11-day1).
Attempts 17 and 18 hit the same ~29,000 plateau with unemployment 11-14% and hundreds of empty dense homes. Attempt 19 goes back to light homes inside the mixed layout so jobs can keep up.
Tax controller: homes 7 -> 4 (demand 0), shops 7 -> 4 (demand 0), factories 7 -> 3 (demand 0)
Day one (restart): dense homes with a 2x2 park in every home cell, factories, shops, coal plant, 12 river pumps, road+rail links. Audit passed.
Restarted attempt 19 on Jan 2000 after the first build landed at half scale (zoom had not taken). New plan: dense homes with parks inside every home block for land value, and a jobs-first alarm.

a20-2003 put a park on the y30 power line, cutting power to the new factory strip x110-114. Audit caught it before the clock ran. Moved the park and added a plan check that refuses parks on lines/roads.
Loan #2 (Feb 2001) and blocks 3-4: dense homes with parks, shops, factory strip x110-114.
Tax controller: homes 4 -> 5 (demand 1883), shops 4 -> 5 (demand 2000), factories 3 -> 4 (demand 59)
Jul 2002: 5,780 people - the fastest start yet, homes still in demand. Ran out of water and power, so loan #3 pays for a coal plant and 19 north riverbank pumps.

District 5 police was blocked by its own home zone and a park tile (plan clash); cleared and built it. Block 3's police (94,36) never got built for the same reason and homes now stand there; dropped it. build.py now refuses parks overlapping planned buildings.
Tax controller: homes 5 -> 6 (demand 331), shops 5 -> 6 (demand 2000), factories 4 -> 5 (demand 2000)
Turned on the four finance ordinances (+$173/yr) and City Beautification ($19/yr, raises land value - fits the tower plan).
Zoo at (110,56) in May 2003 (home demand already ~0 at 10,550 people: the recreation cap).
May 2003: 10,550 people, the fastest growth of any attempt. Turned on finance ordinances + City Beautification and built the zoo early because home demand hit zero.
Tax controller: shops 6 -> 7 (demand 2000), factories 5 -> 6 (demand 2000)
Skipped the planned home tax rise to 7% at 15,900 people: home demand is -317 and upgrades to big buildings need positive demand.
Tax controller: shops 7 -> 8 (demand 1990), factories 6 -> 7 (demand 2000)
Tax controller: shops 8 -> 9 (demand 1988), factories 7 -> 8 (demand 2000)
East homes build: roads y20/y55 and line x127 on the map edge started 4 neighbour deals ($1,000 each, $3,900 surprise). build.py now refuses edge tiles unless --edge-ok.
Tax controller: factories 8 -> 9 (demand 2000)
Tax controller: homes 6 -> 7 (demand -23)
Dec 2006: bond payments $2,599/yr vs taxes $2,095 + ordinances $306 -> about -$600/yr with $68 cash. Homes tax 6 -> 7 (home demand ~0, unemployment 2%).
Deferred the airport and second seaport to 24,000 people: cash $68 and the budget is about -$600/yr; the east factory land is still filling.
Dec 2006: 21,110 people, best year-6 of all attempts. Money is the problem: six loans cost $2,599/yr vs $2,400 income. Home tax up to 7%; airport waits until 24,000.
Big parks ($150 each, 3x3): four next to the north homes at x93-95 y1-13 - testing the home cap (+3,000 each) and land value. build.py has a new bigpark step.
Jul 2007: shop land short and home demand slightly negative with 3% unemployment - empty east home rows x123-126 y24-33 rezoned as dense shops (jobs first).
Dec 2007: 23,030 people; dense factories fill within months. New dense factory row x60-75 y70-72 facing the west homes ($578).

Jul 2008: 24,510 people, cash $205. Airport deferred again (to 28,000). Tax ceiling 10% for factories (demand ~1,900). Homes: 392 tiles in 2x2 buildings and ~100 in 3x3; mean land value 78, 134 tiles at 96+.
Jul 2008: 24,510 people. The parks are working slowly - about half the home land is now 2x2 buildings and a few towers - but money is the limit: seven loans eat almost all the tax.

Dec 2008 loan #8: stadium (101,98), east district homes x110-114 (around a pond) + dense factories x117-121. Plan left line gaps at road crossings and unjoined pipes; audit caught it before the clock ran, fixed.
Tax controller: factories 9 -> 10 (demand 1684)
Jun 2009: spare water 3% -> 7 pumps on the north lake shore x108-114 y19 ($1,785; pipes under the road/buildings cost more than estimated).
Nov 2009 loan #9: airport x106-111 y98-101 ($6,024) - shops stalled 6 months at demand +1,210 with empty land (shop cap). Second seaport still waits.
Nov 2009: 28,510 people, home demand +721 (positive again). Built the airport with loan #9 because shops had stalled for half a year.
Feb 2010: south district x76-100 y98-109, no industry: dense homes + parks west/east, dense shops in the middle ($3,308).
Jul 2010: spare water 6% -> 4 riverbank pumps (73,91) and (73-75,99) for $426; cash now ~$14.
Tax controller: homes 7 -> 8 (demand 1004), shops 9 -> 10 (demand 1798)
Tax controller: homes 8 -> 9 (demand 1063)
Jul 2011 loan #10: fourth coal plant (68,52), 3 lake pumps (110-112,6), dense shop block x102-107 y104-108 ($5,192).
Jul 2011: 32,180 people - best since attempt 2. Home demand +1,000, taxes now 9-10%. Loan #10 for power, lake pumps and a shop block.
Tax controller: homes 9 -> 10 (demand 1148)
Tax controller: factories 10 -> 9 (demand -811)
Tax controller: factories 9 -> 8 (demand -775)

Jul 2012: shop land short -> dense shop cells around the pond (x94-99 y77-82) and x102-107 y110-114 ($809). Factory tax 10 -> 8 with a per-zone ceiling of 8 (factory demand fell to -800 at 10%, as in attempt 13).
Tax controller: homes 10 -> 9 (demand 76)
Feb 2013: spare water 7% -> 5 more lake pumps (107,1-3),(114,3-4) for $579. Home tax 10 -> 9 (demand fell to +76).
Tax controller: factories 8 -> 7 (demand -460)
Tax controller: shops 10 -> 9 (demand -729)
Tax controller: shops 9 -> 8 (demand -998)

Feb 2015 loan #11: six police stations (56,63) (102,17) (79,29) (103,49) (103,92) (118,44); four replaced 3x3 factory patches in high-crime blocks. Home crime averaged 51 (about -18 land value); the one existing station took its area to 0-5. Cleared 7 rubble tiles.
2015: plateau at ~36,000 (record for Claudeville 3). Diagnosis: land value 73 on homes, crime costs ~18 points. Six police stations to push homes past 96 (large apartments).
Tax controller: shops 8 -> 7 (demand -659)
Feb 2017 loan #12: south-east checkerboard district x109-125 y77-96 + east-edge homes x123-125 y57-75 ($4,834; city had 8 empty home and 0 factory tiles). Second seaport x59-62 y49-53.
Jun 2018: 37,780 people (record). Spare water 6% -> 5 more lake pumps ($554); 69 pumps in all.
Jun 2018: 37,780 people - a new Claudeville 3 record. The south-east district and second seaport restarted growth (+2,400 in a year).

Mar 2020 loan #13: south district x109-125 y98-117 with zoo #2 (117,98), alternating shop/home cells ($6,233). The airport did not carry power to line x109 (audit caught it); joined it to line x116 along y103.
A calibration test road landed on the map edge at (76,127) and started a $1,000 neighbour deal. center.sh now records the target tile and autocal skips spots that may fall within 3 tiles of the edge.
Aug 2020: spare water 9% -> 5 riverbank pumps x70 y103-107 (74 pumps in all).
Tax controller: shops 7 -> 8 (demand 2000)
Aug 2021 loan #14: fifth coal plant (72,48); pond district x76-99 y110-125 - homes around the ponds, dense shops y117-121, homes y123-125 ($7,841).
Tax controller: shops 8 -> 9 (demand 1954)
Tax controller: shops 9 -> 10 (demand 1954)
Nov 2022 loan #15: dense factory strip x110-125 y119-124 below the south homes ($1,229). Tax ceilings raised (homes 10, shops 11, factories 9): all demand bars above +1,000, budget about -$2,100/yr.
Tax controller: homes 9 -> 10 (demand 1189), factories 7 -> 8 (demand 1047)
Tax controller: shops 10 -> 8 (demand -1362)
Dec 2023: 48,410 peak (Jul). Spare water 7% -> 14 riverbank pumps y28-41 ($1,647; 88 pumps). Shop tax 10 -> 8, ceiling 9 (shop demand fell to -1,362).
Tax controller: shops 8 -> 7 (demand -1197)
Nov 2025 loan #16: north-east homes x116-125 y1-19 with a big park ($1,968). Power gaps behind the parks (audit caught them) fixed with lines x126 y1-6 and a crossing at (120,20).
2025: passed 50,000 people (peak 51,990) - halfway, with 25 years left. Needs ~2,000/yr from here; money is the risk (16 loans).
Tax controller: factories 8 -> 7 (demand -749)
Tax controller: homes 10 -> 9 (demand 333), factories 7 -> 6 (demand -364)

Dec 2027 loan #17: first district WEST of the river x20-40 y48-68 (dense homes + parks, 2 shop cells, 1 factory cell, 8 riverbank pumps). Causeway ($275) on y69 and raised wires ($110) on y68 across the river, chosen by hand from the Select pop-up; build.py now takes the cheapest option itself with --allow-water. Taxes cut to 9/7/6.
Dec 2027: stuck near 51,000 since 2026 with no land left. Crossed the river for the first time: a causeway and raised wires to a new west district, and taxes cut a point to lift demand.
Tax controller: factories 6 -> 7 (demand -262)
Tax controller: factories 7 -> 6 (demand -88)
Jul 2029 loan #18: sixth coal plant (72,52); spare power was 9%. Fixed the tax floor (taxmin 7 from 2006 had pushed factories back to 7%); now 5.
Tax controller: shops 7 -> 6 (demand -377)
Jul 2031 loan #19: marina (68,108); second west district x20-40 y27-47; 11 riverbank pumps y49-59 ($7,663).
Tax controller: factories 6 -> 7 (demand 1101)
Feb 2032 loan #20: dense factory strip x17-19 y28-61 along the west homes ($1,198). Budget 2032: bonds ~$10,000/yr vs taxes $6,153 + ordinances $939.
Tax controller: factories 7 -> 8 (demand 1237)
Mar 2033 loan #21: road x13, dense factories x14-15 and homes x10-12 y28-61; seventh coal plant (30,15) with line x31 ($6,500).
Mar 2033: 64,500 people - growth sped up to ~5,000 a year as the west districts fill. Loans now 21; budget ~-$4,000/yr.
Aug 2033: 66,740 people. West shop band y21-26 x14-39 ($2,119), no loan.
Tax controller: homes 9 -> 10 (demand 1472), shops 6 -> 7 (demand 2000)
Aug 2034 loan #22: south-west block - dense shops x14-26 y70-75, homes x28-39 and around the lake, stadium #2 (14,77) ($8,253).
Aug 2034: 71,000 people. Need ~1,800/yr to reach 100,000 by 2050; growing ~4,000-5,000/yr now. 22 loans.
Tax controller: shops 7 -> 8 (demand 2000)

Aug 2035 loan #23: south-west band 2 y84-89 (shops x14-19/x28-33, homes x21-26/x35-39) and 11 west-bank pumps y72-82 ($3,918). Pumps were unpowered (empty zone tiles between line x37 and the crossing; audit caught it) - fixed with line (38-39,74).
Tax controller: shops 8 -> 9 (demand 2000)
Aug 2036 loan #24: eighth coal plant (34,15); south-west band 3 y91-103 ($8,531; cash ran out before 9 pipe tiles on y93, covered by pipe x40).
Tax controller: factories 8 -> 7 (demand -754)
